newsitem.title: USA: Schering-Plough net jumps on sales uptick.
newsitem.headline: Schering-Plough net jumps on sales uptick.

text.p: Schering-Plough Corp said Thursday its first quarter 1997 earnings per share jumped 16 percent to $1.03 versus $0.89 the same period last year, fueled by sharply higher U.S. and worldwide sales.
The drug company reported net income of $375 million for the quarter ending March 31, versus $327 million in 1996.

First quarter sales reached $1.6 billion, 13 percent higher than last year, the company said, although the negative foreign exchange impact of a stronger U.S. dollar diminished the 1997 sales comparison by about three percentage points.
"Schering-Plough achieved a solid performance in the first quarter, led by strong gains in our worldwide pharmaceuticals business," said Richard Jay Kogan, president and chief executive officer.
"All of the company's major business components -- worldwide pharmaceuticals, animal health and HealthCare Products -- recorded higher sales versus the prior year," he said.

"We look for 1997 to be another year of good earnings growth, as we continue to strengthen our worldwide market presence and grow our product pipeline through internal research efforts and outside alliances," Kogan said.
In the quarter, worldwide ethical pharmaceutical sales grew by 14 percent, with growth led by Claritin antihistamines and Intron A, an antiviral/anticancer agent, the company said.
Schering-Plough said first quarter worldwide sales of Claritin, the world's best-selling antihistamine, jumped 49 percent to $353 million, while sales of INTRON A rose 19 percent to $143 million.
The company said U.S. sales of prescription pharmaceuticals improved 21 percent in the first quarter.

But competition with generic brands resulted in lower U.S. sales for its albuterol asthma therapies, with U.S. branded competition also causing lower sales for Eulexin, a prostate cancer treatment, Schering-Plough said.

It said international ethical pharmaceutical sales rose six percent in the first quarter, with growth led by Claritin, Intron A, Losec, an anti-ulcer agent, and Elocon, a medium-potency topical steroid.

First quarter 1997 sales in the company's worldwide animal health business bolted 30 percent higher, it said, largely from growing sales of Nuflor, a broad-spectrum antibiotic for bovine respiratory disease.
Sales for Schering-Plough HealthCare Products increased six percent in the 1997 first quarter, the company said.
"Schering-Plough's major businesses are performing well, achieving solid gains in both our U.S. and international markets," Kogan said.
